chunks: Al-Halabi said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
about the game which a man strikes with a sword, or stabs with a spear, or shoots with an arrow, killing it, having invoked the name of God (Bismillah) when he did so
So he said: Eat, there is no problem with it.

key_terms.الصَّيْدِ: game/hunt — refers to wild animals killed through hunting; its permissibility depends on proper tasmiyyah (invoking God's name)
key_terms.سَمَّى: to invoke the name of God (Bismillah) — a required condition for the permissibility of slaughter and hunting
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no problem with it — a standard jurisprudential formula indicating permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is game killed by sword, spear, or arrow permissible to eat in Islam if Bismillah was recited?
ai.summary: Al-Halabi (Ubayd Allah ibn Ali al-Halabi) poses a jurisprudential question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the permissibility of eating game killed through conventional weapons — sword, spear, or arrow — when Bismillah was recited at the moment of the hunt. The Imam's response is unambiguous: it is permissible to eat such game. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh on hunting (sayd), affirming that the invocation of God's name (tasmiyyah) is the essential condition, regardless of the weapon type used.
